title: Saffron Insights - MLOps handoff / integration scratchpad
content:
Call summary (2025-01-18) - intro + scope:
- Intro: Initial technical sync with Saffron Insights (data science lead = Priya Menon, infra = Tomas Reilly). Goal: move their vector-search-backed recommendation pipeline from a PoC (single-node inference in EKS) to a Redwood Private deployment (VPC) with predictable latency and secure keys.
- Main ask: 99th percentile latencies < 120ms for single-user recalls, steady-state qps = 120 req/s, peak burst to 400 req/s for 3-5 minutes.
- Data constraints: PII in user attributes, but vectors are derived from hashed IDs + embeddings; customer wants us to treat vectors as regulated PHI-equivalent (needs audit trail + KMS).

Key architecture notes (sketch):
- Ingest: existing Kafka pipeline -> offline embedding generation (PyTorch) -> s3-compatible object store (minio in their corp cloud) for shard storage.
- Serving: Redwood Private in customer VPC. Two pools: cpu pre-processing (small EC2) + GPU pool (A10G equivalents) for large-model rerank/recall.
- Cache: prefix KV cache for common queries (they have ~8k hot users). Suggest TTL-based cache + invalidate on profile update webhooks.
- Route policy: prefer on-prem GPU until utilization > 70% then fallback to hosted dedicated model for overflow (they asked if Redwood supports multi-tier fallback -> yes, demonstrate).

Constraints & gotchas the customer called out:
1) MDS (model data store) retention: compliance requires 90-day access logs and immutable write-once flags for embeddings older than 7 days. Need to map to Redwood audit log retention settings and confirm immutable-store compatibility.
2) Key rotation: corporate KMS rotates keys monthly; they need HSM/KMS integration and zero-copy retrieval of encrypted KV cache. Check compatibility with their vendor (VenariKMS) - engineering to confirm.
3) Network egress policy: all calls must stay within their VPC + company proxies. They will not allow direct internet egress from workers. Implication: any fallback to Redwood-hosted endpoint must flow through an approved NAT/proxy or we need dedicated private link.
4) Quantization: DS team wants int8 to save memory but is worried about regression on rerank quality. Plan: A/B compare quantized variant on small prompt sets; Redwood Optimize recommended configs should help.

Performance planning numbers (customer-provided):
- Model: proprietary 7B transformer for rerank (seq_len 256).
- Median tokens per request = 18, avg prompt tokens = 26, generated tokens minimal (0-8).
- Target TTFB: <70ms for winner route; 99p <120ms overall.
- Memory budget: 40GB per GPU node (they want to avoid multi-GPU splits).
- Desired throughput per GPU: ~100 qps with batching (but prefer latency over batching for key endpoints).

Action items (assigned):
- [Rhea] Draft runbook section for VPC-only deployment & egress options (due 2025-01-22).
- [Elliot] Validate VenariKMS HSM compatibility with Redwood Private (open ticket to infra: INF-2049) (due 2025-01-24).
- [Samira] Run quick eval: int8 quant vs fp16 on our internal rerank testset and produce delta report (due 2025-01-28).
- [Tomas / Saffron] Provide representative latency traces + typical query distribution histogram (expected by 2025-01-21).
- [Rhea -> Solutions] Prep a short demo sequence showing fallback to hosted-dedicated when VPC pool is saturated (demo date requested: 2025-01-30).

Open questions (need answers before design freeze):
- Can Saffron accept a small agent in their VPC that forwards overflow traffic to Redwood via PrivateLink, or do they require all compute to stay strictly on-prem? (affects cost + timeline)
- For audit logs: do they require per-request signed attestations or is a centralized audit trail sufficient? Need to sync with legal/compliance.
- Is there any regulatory requirement that prohibits ephemeral storage (e.g., local disk caches) on GPU nodes? If yes, we must enable disk encryption and revocation on node teardown.

Risk register (short):
- High: Key management mismatch - if VenariKMS not compatible, Private deploy timeline slips. Mitigation: plan alternate KMS or hardware proxy.
- Medium: Latency regression from quantization. Mitigation: gating via canary rollout + per-prompt quality checks.
- Low: Saffron's Kafka topology has strict partitioning that may produce hot shards; may need sharding advice.

Notes-to-self / fragments: 
- Idea: precompute top-100 candidate set offline daily; use model rerank only for top-10 to reduce QPS on GPU. Need to estimate freshness vs business rules.
- Consider batch size tuning: for low-latency endpoints, continuous batching with max latency 15ms may help. Will propose two profiles: 15ms latency-target low-batch / 80ms high-batch for cost optimization.
- Discuss possibility of 'embedding rotation' where older vectors are compressed and moved to cold storage to reduce hot-store size.

Meeting prep for next 1:1 with Priya (2025-01-21):
- Bring blackout scenarios: what happens if VPC pool loses 2 GPUs? will they accept degraded throughput or must failover to hosted?
- Get confirmation on retention policy for logs/embeddings.
- Two migration windows options: "big bang" (2 weeks) vs phased (region-by-region). Customer leans phased.

Demo checklist (for 2025-01-30 demo):
- VPC-only baseline: show 120 qps sustained with 99p <120ms.
- Simulate peak burst to 400 qps -> demonstrate automatic routing to hosted fallback (metrics show seamless failover).
- Show KMS key usage & rotation logs (test key, not production).
- Show canary rollout: quantized variant vs FP16 with perf/quality delta.

Closing note: this is high-value logosize; security + SLA are top priorities. Keep proposal conservative on cost estimations; emphasize predictable costs for steady-state and options for burst credits.

Revision log:
- 2025-01-20: added detailed action items after follow-up email from Priya.
- 2025-01-24: updated risk register after Elliot confirmed partial KMS compatibility (still validating edge cases).
